h: Getting the Most From a Canterbury Night
p: Canterbury is a proper university city as well as a pilgrimage one, with the University of Kent up on the hill and Canterbury Christ Church right in town. That gives the place a youthful buzz that sits alongside all the medieval stonework, and it's that mix of old streets and young energy that makes a games bar feel right at home here.

Getting into the centre is easy. Canterbury West and Canterbury East stations both sit just outside the old walls, and high-speed trains link the city with London in around an hour. If you're coming by car, the park and ride sites are worth knowing about, as the historic centre is tight on space.

For a group booking, a bit of planning keeps things smooth. Agree numbers early, give everyone a rough idea of timings, and pick one person to keep the booking details. Divide into fair teams, and if there's a birthday or celebration, make the guest of honour captain for the night. It's surprising how competitive people get once there's a title at stake.

If you want to stretch the trip, the coast is close. Whitstable, famous for its oysters and harbour, is a short drive or bus ride north, and makes a lovely afternoon by the sea. The Canterbury Roman Museum, built around the remains of a Roman townhouse floor, is another interesting stop in the centre. And the Marlowe Theatre, named after the city's own playwright Christopher Marlowe, puts on big touring shows if you fancy a different kind of evening.
